text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said it was maintaining its outperform rating on Brazilian state-run telecommunications firm Telebras TBR,N and its $180 target price.

-- "We believe yesterday's news reporting that Telebras is taking steps to make extra tariff cuts is dubious and that the share selloff this news prompted was unwarranted," analyst Luiz Carvalho said in a report.
-- Investors should use yesterday's share weakness as a buying opportunity, given the flimsy nature of the news in question, Carvalho said.

-- On Thursday, a Telebras director said the company was preparing to cut rates to meet competition from private service providers. "Telebras is under pressure to reduce its tariffs given the new spirit of competition in the market," the company's director of Services, Daltron Magalhaes, told reporters.
-- Carvalho said "Telebras completed a rate rebalancing process earlier this year, the net effect of which was highly positive for the company."

-- "In our view, there is little reason to believe that any additional steps over the next few years would be negative for Telebras and, as it stands, the company's long-distance rates are relatively competitive," he added.
-- Telebras preferred was down 7.48 percent at 135.80 reais.
